final_recommendation: The room converged on a negotiated settlement pathway: FINMA commits to a statutory amendment locking AT1 hierarchy prospectively (text by Tuesday, public Friday), plus a UBS claims framework specifying pro-rata recovery tied to acquisition economics with 60-day eligibility determinations. Bondholders conditionally pause Friday filing pending amendment review. The settlement hinges on pre-briefing rating agencies Wednesday-Thursday to isolate Credit Suisse as exceptional (viability trigger timing, negative equity, one-time acquisition structure) before the Friday public statement.
minority_objections: Bondholder counsel initially demanded full reversal of write-down and threatened three-jurisdiction litigation if FINMA delayed
Insurance observer pressed for Federal indemnity structure commitment by EOD, warning decade-long tail pricing if Federal couldn't commit Friday
key_conflicts: Authority boundary: FINMA cannot commit Federal indemnity structure to 90-day adjudication timeline without inter-agency coordination
Recovery methodology: bondholders demanded fixed formula (pro-rata equity upside) versus FINMA's initial offer of process framework only
Timing pressure: bondholder Friday filing deadline versus FINMA's need for parliamentary approval and Federal coordination
key_concessions: FINMA commits to statutory amendment locking AT1 hierarchy prospectively (not just policy memo)
FINMA coordinates UBS claims framework with pro-rata recovery formula tied to acquisition economics, published Friday
Bondholders pause Friday filing pending 48-hour review of amendment text
FINMA agrees to pre-brief rating agencies Wednesday-Thursday to isolate Credit Suisse as exceptional case
red_lines: Bondholders: will file Monday if Friday statement lacks specific recovery formula (not discretionary case-by-case)
FINMA: cannot reverse write-down or commit Federal indemnity authority unilaterally
Insurance carriers: will lock decade-long tail pricing if no process visibility on Credit Suisse claims by Friday
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Parliamentary approval timeline for statutory amendment remains uncertain beyond 'Friday' commitment
Federal indemnity structure's actual capacity to commit to 90-day adjudication window never confirmed
Cross-border litigation risk (US/EU/UK jurisdictions) discussed early but abandoned once settlement pathway emerged
Reputational damage to Swiss regulatory framework and director liability beyond immediate claims tail
downstream_risk_variables: Rating agency reception to three-ground isolation narrative (viability trigger timing, negative equity, acquisition structure)
Market repricing speed: whether Deutsche and other AT1 stabilize Monday or continue distressed trading
UBS's willingness to honor pro-rata recovery formula if acquisition economics deteriorate post-announcement
Litigation tail duration if Federal cannot deliver 90-day timeline or if bondholders reject amendment language Tuesday
uncertainty_notes: Federal indemnity structure's Friday commitment remained unconfirmed at meeting end (FINMA promised yes/no by 5pm but call not completed). Parliamentary approval process for statutory amendment discussed but timeline beyond 'Friday' not locked. Pro-rata recovery formula agreed in principle but actual percentage calculation methodology (acquisition price basis, eligible principal denominator) not finalized. Rating agency pre-briefing committed but content/timing of Wednesday-Thursday sessions not specified.

marker_evidence.litigation_likelihood: Litigation threat drove early rounds (Friday filing deadline, three-jurisdiction suit) but was conditionally paused once FINMA committed to statutory amendment and UBS claims framework. Remained live backstop, not dominant outcome.
marker_evidence.regulatory_legitimacy_challenge: FINMA's ordinance timing and viability-event basis challenged in R1-R2 (retroactivity claims, emergency law change), but room shifted to prospective amendment rather than sustained attack on March write-down legality.
marker_evidence.creditor_hierarchy_controversy: Hierarchy inversion (equity preserved, AT1 wiped) was the central, driving concern across all rounds—shaped amendment demand, recovery formula negotiation, and rating agency isolation strategy. Dominated room direction.
marker_evidence.market_confidence_damage: AT1 repricing contagion (Deutsche at 40 cents, sector-wide premium increases) drove settlement structure—rating agency pre-briefing, three-ground isolation, pro-rata formula all designed to contain market panic. Central thread.
marker_evidence.claims_tail: Multi-year tail (decade-long D&O repricing, discovery costs, settlement reserves) was the primary lever bondholders and insurers used to force FINMA concessions. Shaped UBS framework demand, Federal timeline push, and Friday announcement structure.
marker_evidence.financial_lines_relevance: D&O/E&O carrier repricing and director/adviser exposure surfaced repeatedly (R2-R8) as concrete pressure point, but was instrumental rather than decision-driving—used to justify settlement terms, not independently developed as structured risk.
